extracts.lead_summary: The floor hunt reached the round number and went through it. XLU closed $39.51 (-3.7%) after trading as low as $39.13 — the first trip below $40 since 2024 — on the week the 10Y closed at 5.18%, a 19-year high, and the 30Y touched 5.40%. But the week's real story is the inversion: for six weeks the nuclear pair led the sector down, and this week it finally said no — CEG +3.4%, VST -1.4%, against a regulated complex that lost 3–5% across the board. Natural gas ripped ~10% to $3.25 on the AI-power bid, Oracle declared force majeure on a data center because it couldn't get power, and the market remembered what CEG and VST actually sell. The income case is still dead at -235bp. The scarcity case just came back from the dead.
